instruction.text: Look closely. What can you see? Piece the words together.

atoms.b: Human beings have two eyes, which are protected within the ((++eye_sockets eye_make-up)).
The ((++colourful black)) part of the eye is called the iris. This name comes from the ancient Greek word for 'rainbow'.

end.text: The most common eye colours are brown, blue and grey. Did you know that over 90% of all people have brown eyes? On the other hand, green eyes are the rarest - only about 2% of people in the world have them.

atoms.b: The pupil is the hole in the centre of the iris. ((++Light Sound)) shines into the eye through this hole.
When it’s ((++dark cold)) or gloomy, the pupil expands so that more light can enter the eye. When it’s bright, the pupil shrinks and lets in less ((++light moisture)).

Light-sensitive cells within the eye receive light and send information about its pattern to the ((++brain heart)) via the optic nerve. The brain uses signals sent from both eyes to make an image. That is how we ((++see hear)).

The eye is extremely sensitive and needs to protect itself. The eyebrows and ((++eyelashes nerves)) keep out dust and ((++sweat frost)). To protect your eyes from foreign bodies and bright lights, you can close them using your ((++eyelids eyebrows)).

instruction.text: Match the threat with the form of protection.
